# Results — Study 62 (Premium-Seller): covered-call income vs the index, 2014–2026

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly total returns of **QYLD** (Global X
Nasdaq-100 Covered Call), its underlying **QQQ**, and **SPY**, Yahoo, 2014–2026. Inputs fingerprint
`48f465a73194`.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Covered-call income beats the index"? `BUSTED`

The "income" pitch — sell calls, collect premium, get superior equity exposure — is a `MIRAGE`. QYLD
trailed its *own* underlying (QQQ) by a staggering **−10.9%/yr (Sharpe −1.05, t −3.6)**: **+8.1%/yr vs
+19.3%**, and below SPY too. The reason is a brutal asymmetry: writing calls keeps only **50% of QQQ's
up months** but still suffers **58% of its down months** — you cap the gains *more* than the premium
cushions the losses. The monthly distributions look like income; on total return you've sold your upside
for a payment that doesn't cover it. `BUSTED`.

## Data stamp

- **Panel**: QYLD vs QQQ (underlying) vs SPY, monthly total return, 2014–2026, 150 months, fingerprint
  `48f465a73194`

## QYLD trailed its own underlying by ~11%/yr

| | CAGR | Sharpe | vol | max-DD |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QYLD (covered call) | +8.1% | **0.76** | 11.0% | −23% |
| QQQ (the underlying it holds) | +19.3% | **1.06** | 18.3% | −33% |
| SPY (market) | +13.6% | 0.94 | 14.9% | −24% |
| spread QYLD − QQQ | **−10.9%/yr** | −1.05 | — | — |

A fund that *owns* QQQ and writes calls on it underperformed QQQ itself by 11 points a year, at a lower
Sharpe. The premium it collects is real cash, but it's dwarfed by the upside it forgoes — and the
high-yield distribution is largely return *of* capital, not return *on* it.

## The asymmetry that sinks it

| | QYLD | QQQ |
|---|---|---|
| mean return in QQQ-up months | +2.4% | +4.7% |
| mean return in QQQ-down months | −2.2% | −3.8% |
| **upside capture** | **50%** | — |
| **downside capture** | **58%** | — |

This is the whole story. A covered call truncates the right tail (you keep ~half the up moves) while the
premium only slightly buffers the left tail (you still take ~58% of the down moves). Capturing *more* of
the downside than the upside is the opposite of what you want — and over a rising market it compounds
into an 11%/yr shortfall.

## The honest takeaway

Covered-call "income" funds are a `MIRAGE`: QYLD trailed its own underlying by ~11%/yr at a lower Sharpe,
because selling calls caps 50% of the upside while leaving 58% of the downside. The fat monthly
distribution feels like income, but you've financed it by selling your gains. `NONE` signal, `MIRAGE`
tradability, the income-beats-the-index claim `BUSTED`.
